description: Cross-repo drift gate for the D7 reserved-tag rule (ADR oci_index_only_dispatch, D7:319). Both crates/ocx_lib's Tag::is_reserved (Rust) and the bot's reserved-tag predicate (Python) must reproduce this exact verdict table. Per meta-plan_oci_index_alignment.md §10.3, the reserved-canonical-form rule here is deliberately widened beyond D7:319's sha256-only text to cover Algorithm::ALL = {sha256, sha384, sha512} -- reservation and addressability are different questions, and only reservation widens; addressability stays sha256-only pending N-12. A new row is a shared-fixture change reviewed on both sides; a new key on a case is a schema change reviewed on both sides. `why` is documentation only, never asserted.

cases.why: wrong hex length, not a digest alias
canonical digest alias, sha384 -- an implementation hardcoded to sha256 fails this row

canonical digest alias, sha512 -- an implementation hardcoded to sha256 fails this row. Note: this tag is 135 chars ("sha512." + 128 hex), exceeding the OCI tag grammar's 128-char max (schema/root.schema.json ^[a-zA-Z0-9_][a-zA-Z0-9._-]{0,127}$), so it can never appear as an actual tag from a registry -- the verdict here documents the reserved-canonical-form rule's own logic, not a reachable input
prefix matches sha384, but hex length is sha256's -- catches a prefix-only check
